title: Typed stream contracts, compact checkpoints, and safe retry patterns for Python SDK
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: define a compact, low-allocation typed contract for streaming LLM responses that supports: incremental typed hydration (pydantic/dataclass), deterministic chunk reassembly, checkpoint markers for idempotent retries, and ergonomic examples for customers. This ticket produces a reference implementation, tests, and a short cookboook for SDK users.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A small runtime module (<= 200 lines) that exposes a StreamContract class with: marker-based checkpoints, deterministic chunk concatenation semantics, and a lightweight hydrator path for pydantic/dataclass models. 2) Unit tests covering normal streaming, mid-stream retry using checkpoint markers, and malformed chunk recovery. 3) End-to-end example in examples/streaming_retry_demo.py showing client-side resume + server fallback. 4) Docs and a short API migration guide for existing streaming helpers.
notes: Design constraints: keep allocations minimal (avoid building whole event lists), make checkpoints orthogonal to model shape, and provide a best-effort reassembly that tolerates partial tokens and out-of-order deltas. We decided not to ship a generic compression layer in this iteration to keep the API surface small.
decisions: 1) Checkpoints will be opaque string tokens emitted by the server and validated by the SDK; SDK stores the latest checkpoint and resumes by including 'resume_from' in the next request. 2) Use marker events instead of sequence-indexed frames to tolerate minor reorderings from proxies. 3) Streaming union types: represent as top-level discriminator field (e.g., 'type': 'delta'|'final'|'checkpoint') to simplify hydrators.
implementation_plan: - Phase A (this ticket): implement StreamContract, CompactCheckpoint, and two hydrators: DataclassHydrator and PydanticHydrator. - Phase B (follow-up): integrate with streaming backpressure APIs and batching runtime. - Tests and examples published to examples/streaming_retry_demo.py and docs/streaming-retries.md.
risks: - Server-side must adopt checkpoint token emission; temporary compatibility shim included but not ideal. - Edge-case: if server emits incorrect checkpoint sequence, client must fall back to conservative full-retry which increases cost. - Interop: other SDK languages need to adopt same marker convention to support cross-language streaming handoffs.
code_snippet_examples:
Example: 
from redwood import StreamContract, PydanticHydrator

contract = StreamContract(schema='ChatDelta')
contract.add_checkpoint_handler(lambda token: store_checkpoint(token))

for event in client.stream(req):
    if event['type'] == 'checkpoint':
        contract.handle_checkpoint(event['token'])
    else:
        obj = PydanticHydrator.hydrate(event)
        consume(obj)

# On resume: client includes last_seen_checkpoint in headers to resume from that point
